entries.text: Building a full-stack learning tracker from scratch: Python fundamentals (control flow, functions, dicts vs. lists, debugging real tracebacks, loop-variable scoping, migration scripts), reading and fixing my own logic bugs (premature returns inside loops, mutable vs. immutable updates, name-before-assignment errors), designing a data model where derived values (progress) are never stored but recomputed from a log of evidence, working with an LLM API under JSON-schema-constrained structured output, building a REST API with FastAPI (routes, async/await, CORS, request/response bodies), and building a React frontend (useState, useEffect, prop threading, controlled inputs, fetch/promises, the Rules of Hooks) that talks to that backend over HTTP — plus enough of the surrounding ecosystem (git branches and history, npm/Node tooling, Obsidian plugin installation, force-directed graph rendering with SVG) to ship the whole thing end to end.

concepts.name: Python
concepts.summary: A programming language used to build applications and implement control-flow logic.

concepts.name: for loop
concepts.summary: A control-flow structure that repeats a block of code for each item in a sequence or range.

concepts.name: nested for loops
concepts.summary: A for loop placed inside another for loop to process combinations or multidimensional data.

concepts.name: dovetail joint
concepts.summary: A woodworking joint that interlocks fan-shaped pins and tails to join pieces of wood securely.

concepts.name: hand sawing
concepts.summary: A woodworking technique for cutting material manually with a handsaw along a controlled path.

concepts.name: FastAPI
concepts.summary: FastAPI is a Python web framework for building backend APIs.

concepts.name: TypeScript
concepts.summary: TypeScript is a typed programming language used to build the journal's frontend.

concepts.name: backend
concepts.summary: A backend handles server-side logic, data access, and API requests for an application.

concepts.name: frontend
concepts.summary: A frontend provides the user-facing interface through which people interact with an application.

concepts.name: AI journal
concepts.summary: An AI journal is an application for recording, organizing, and potentially reflecting on personal experiences with AI assistance.

concepts.name: API
concepts.summary: An API defines how the frontend and backend exchange data and functionality.

concepts.name: separation of concerns
concepts.summary: Dividing responsibilities between AI and application code so each handles the work it is best suited for.

concepts.name: debugging
concepts.summary: Systematically identifying and fixing the causes of unexpected software behavior.

concepts.name: stack trace
concepts.summary: A diagnostic record showing the sequence of function calls that led to a crash or error.

concepts.name: Git hygiene
concepts.summary: Maintaining a clean, understandable version-control history through practices such as focused commits and avoiding unnecessary changes.

concepts.name: hard invariants
concepts.summary: Hard invariants are non-negotiable rules that code enforces regardless of a model's output.

concepts.name: AI guardrails
concepts.summary: AI guardrails constrain model outputs by combining model judgment with deterministic checks for safety and correctness.

concepts.name: TypeError
concepts.summary: A TypeError occurs when an operation or function receives a value of an inappropriate type, such as arguments that no longer match a function signature.

concepts.name: NameError
concepts.summary: A NameError occurs when code refers to a variable or name that is not defined in the current scope.

concepts.name: function signatures
concepts.summary: A function signature defines the parameters a function accepts, and stale calls can cause runtime errors when the signature changes.

concepts.name: variable scope
concepts.summary: Variable scope determines where a name is defined and accessible, making scope mistakes especially important when tracing nested loops.

concepts.name: .gitignore
concepts.summary: A .gitignore file prevents specified files, such as local secrets, from being added to Git tracking in the first place.

concepts.name: tracked files
concepts.summary: A file can remain tracked by Git even after being added to .gitignore, so it must be explicitly removed from the index.

concepts.name: history rewriting
concepts.summary: Rewriting Git history is necessary for removing a secret from already-pushed commits, but is usually unnecessary when the repository was never pushed to a remote.

concepts.name: custom URI schemes
concepts.summary: Custom URI schemes let an application or operating system route specially formatted links to an external app.

concepts.name: os.startfile
concepts.summary: Python’s os.startfile launches a file, URL, or registered URI using the operating system’s associated handler.

concepts.name: URL encoding
concepts.summary: URL encoding safely escapes characters such as spaces and punctuation so values can be embedded in URI components.

concepts.name: import side effects
concepts.summary: Module-level Python code executes during import, so any actions there occur each time the module is imported or reloaded.

concepts.name: list
concepts.summary: A Python list stores the sequence of goals that the for loop processes.

concepts.name: off-by-one error
concepts.summary: An off-by-one error occurs when iteration starts or stops one position too early or too late, such as skipping the final item.

concepts.name: embeddings
concepts.summary: Embeddings represent text or other data as numerical vectors that capture semantic relationships.

concepts.name: retrieval-augmented generation
concepts.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation improves large language model responses by retrieving relevant external information before generating an answer.

concepts.name: large language models
concepts.summary: Large language models generate and transform text by learning statistical patterns from extensive training data.

concepts.name: Model Context Protocol
concepts.summary: Model Context Protocol is a standard for connecting AI models to external tools and data sources.

concepts.name: model weights
concepts.summary: Model weights are learned numerical parameters that encode patterns and capabilities in a machine learning model.

concepts.name: AI
concepts.summary: Artificial intelligence refers to systems that perform tasks involving capabilities such as learning, reasoning, language understanding, and generation.

concepts.name: sorting
concepts.summary: Sorting arranges the elements of a collection according to a specified ordering.

concepts.name: custom key function
concepts.summary: A custom key function computes the comparison value used to determine each element’s position during sorting.

concepts.name: dictionary
concepts.summary: A Python dictionary stores key-value mappings and is useful for representing structured application data.

concepts.name: derived state
concepts.summary: Derived state is computed from authoritative evidence rather than stored separately, preventing inconsistent progress values.

concepts.name: JSON Schema
concepts.summary: JSON Schema constrains and validates the structure of data exchanged with an LLM API.

concepts.name: async/await
concepts.summary: Async/await enables asynchronous Python or JavaScript code to perform I/O without blocking other work.

concepts.name: React
concepts.summary: React builds interactive frontend interfaces from components whose state and data flow drive the rendered UI.

concepts.name: REST API
concepts.summary: A REST API exposes backend resources through HTTP routes with structured request and response bodies.

concepts.name: control flow
concepts.summary: Control flow determines how a program branches, loops, returns, and executes statements in sequence.

concepts.name: mutable vs. immutable updates
concepts.summary: Mutable updates change existing data in place, while immutable updates create replacement values that make state changes easier to track safely.

concepts.name: migration scripts
concepts.summary: Migration scripts transform existing stored data or schemas so an application can evolve without losing compatibility.

concepts.name: structured output
concepts.summary: Structured output constrains an AI response to a predictable schema that software can validate and consume reliably.

concepts.name: CORS
concepts.summary: CORS is a browser security mechanism that controls which origins may make requests to a backend API.

concepts.name: Rules of Hooks
concepts.summary: The Rules of Hooks require React Hooks to be called consistently at the top level of components or custom Hooks.
